SMTO-EXE-0124 — The chosen computer can't run SMTO's browser this way

GUID: 90436a6c-68dd-5708-88ec-dd49c5168669
Slug: browser-target-capability-missing
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • The computer SMTO is using for this conversation either doesn't have the browser set up, or can't show a visible browser window. Nothing was opened or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check which Gateway this task uses (it is shown under the message box). If you can, switch to one where SMTO's browser has worked before. The browser runs on the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to work on a computer), and not every Gateway has it set up.
  2. If you asked for a visible browser window, ask SMTO to use a background (hidden) browser instead. A visible window needs a computer with a screen and someone signed in to its desktop.
  3. Ask the person who manages the Gateway to rerun its installer and restart it once no tasks are running on it. The installer adds the browser and the system files it needs; turning on the Browser skill alone doesn't install them.
  4. After the repair, open Capabilities next to the message box, select Refresh catalog, then start a new task. Tasks that were already running keep the old list of what the Gateway can do.

What success looks like

  • In a new task, SMTO reports the browser is available on the chosen Gateway and opens a page.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway. Repair the installation in place; don't delete the Gateway's pairing, settings, browser profiles or task files to start over.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected execution target has no browser operation support, does not report the browser capability needed (for example Playwright or Chromium missing, browser disabled), or a headed session was requested without a display.

What this means

  • The selected Gateway client lacks the browser operation interface, or a headed launch was requested without headed-session capability. Other readiness reasons remain distinct categories. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • The selected Gateway client lacks the browser operation interface, or a headed launch was requested without headed-session capability. Other readiness reasons remain distinct categories.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect advertised browser and headed capabilities on the exact selected Gateway and its session.

How to fix it

  • skill.availability reports browser_target_capability_missing when the Gateway client lacks browser_operation or the captured capabilities omit the operation's tag; PlaywrightBackend._start raises it for headless=false without browser_headed (no DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY on Linux). Inspect browser.status. If packages, Chromium or OS libraries are missing, rerun ./install.sh, or ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh (Linux), ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh (macOS) or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 (Windows), as the Gateway's account; after active work settles restart the Gateway, refresh capabilities and start a new task. Check GATEWAY_BROWSER_ENABLED is not false.
  • Inspect browser.status on the selected Gateway. Reinstall or repair that Gateway with its supported installer if browser packages, Chromium or OS libraries are missing. After repair succeeds and active work is settled, restart the Gateway and refresh metadata for a new task. Explicitly disabled browsers, unsupported headed sessions and unconfigured CDP attachments require the corresponding configuration instead.
  • If installation repair is indicated: From the matching repository checkout, run ./install.sh for the server and local Gateway, or use the Gateway-only installer: ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh on Linux, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh on macOS, or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 on Windows. Run it as the account used by the Gateway so its environment and browser caches are repaired.
  • After an installation repair: After active jobs and uncertain operations are reconciled, restart the affected Gateway. Restart the server too if the shared installer updated it. Refresh Gateway metadata before starting a new task.
  • Confirm the reported capability works on the selected Gateway after correcting its diagnosed cause. If installation repair was needed, require the installer checks to pass. Refresh metadata and start a new task when capabilities change; existing tasks keep their captured snapshot.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm the reported capability works on the selected Gateway after correcting its diagnosed cause. If installation repair was needed, require the installer checks to pass. Refresh metadata and start a new task when capabilities change; existing tasks keep their captured snapshot. Inspect prior execution receipts before repeating work.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended target supports the requested browser mode before a new session is started.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.
  • Repair the installation in place; do not delete Gateway pairing, credentials, settings, browser profiles or task artifacts.
  • Granting a Skill permission does not install its dependencies.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
